newsitem.title: CHINA: China 1997 state debt issue aims at individuals.
newsitem.headline: China 1997 state debt issue aims at individuals.

text.p: China's state debt issues this year will focus on furthering reform of the state debt markets and meeting the increasing demand from investors, the Shanghai Securities News said on Thursday.

"The state debt issue in 1997 will focus on actively promoting the construction of the state debt market and aim to satisfy the demand from individual investors," the newspaper quoted deputy finance minister Liu Jibing as saying.
To achieve these goals, the Finance Ministry will issue a record 123 billion yuan in non-tradeable two, three and five-year treasury notes from March 1 to October 20, Liu was quoted as saying.
"The T-notes are aimed at individuals," Liu said.
China issued a record of 195.2 billion yuan in state debt in 1996 and industry sources expect this year's issue to be another record of around 250 billion yuan.
China resumed state debt issues in 1981 and had cumulatively issued a total of 676.5 billion yuan by the end of 1996 with 426.5 billion yuan still outstanding, official figures show. ($1 = 8.3 yuan)
